verdicts.reason: X is a presence check for any place/trade/generational persona framing scored 0 when absent, while Y is a specificity scale that demands a named locality plus counted years plus a tangible asset for a 10 and still awards a 5 to a bare 'as a farmer' affiliation, so scores diverge on both ends.

X requires an actual ongoing formal relationship (advisory seat, permit/grantee history, prior correspondence), whereas Y rewards mere familiarity cues such as naming officials or thanking the agency for coordination, which a first-time commenter can display.
Citing CFR parts and sections is a surface citation practice, while arguing the rule exceeds statutory authority is a substantive legal claim; comments routinely do one without the other.
Both require the commenter's own numeric compliance-cost estimate with its derivation or basis stated, and both score 0 when no figures appear.

X credits any job, ownership position, or operational role even with no place or tenure (e.g. 'as General Counsel of Acme Corp'), while Y requires tenure, residency length, or generational/occupational identity tied to a place or trade.

Both operationalize 'this is a mass-campaign form letter rather than an individualized comment' from the same cues (duplicated wording, stock demands, prewritten phrasing) and both zero out on bespoke text.

X counts ordinary operational and local-identity positioning (a working fisherman, a small-farm owner), while Y requires expert authority credentials such as senior title, licensure, or specialized expertise.

X measures professional drafting register and counsel-style conventions, whereas Y measures precise mapping of proposed text to docket provisions, CFR sections, and requested edits; a polished but broad-brush counsel letter scores high on X and low on Y.
Both score an explicitly disclosed prior or ongoing dealing with the issuing agency (permits, recurring meetings, previous correspondence) and both zero out when no such history is stated.

X requires disclosure of actual prior dealings such as permits or recurring meetings, while Y also fires on thin familiarity signals like naming officials or thanking the agency for coordination with no prior relationship.
Both score the same artifact set (email/portal headers, attachment notices, filenames, OCR defects, duplicated cover text) and both zero out on clean standalone prose.
Both score whether the comment offers a concrete alternative regulatory design specific enough to implement, and both give 0 for pure objection with no proposal.
Both score multi-party representation signaling through member lists, counts of represented organizations, and consensus claims, and both zero out on an evidently individual submission.

X measures disproportionate density of accumulated authorities of any kind including studies and quoted sources, while Y measures precise legal mapping to docket text and CFR provisions; a study-heavy scientific comment scores high on X and low on Y.
First-hand operational experience is an evidentiary content dimension while intensity of expressed feeling is an affective register dimension; either can appear without the other.

Y demands quantified organizational scale, membership, market share, or geographic reach, while X also credits unquantified longevity, assets, facilities, and senior titles, so a 'founded in 1892, signed by our President' letter scores high on X and low on Y.
